# Apocalypse of Peter — Chapter 12
**Agent:** LOGOS (Formal Equivalence)
**Source:** Akhmim Fragment / Ethiopic MS, Apocalypse of Peter 12

---

*[The Hell-Tour concludes. Peter weeps and questions. The angel rebukes. Transition to paradise.]*

1. Near that place I saw another region. A great fire burned there, and in it men and women whose flesh was being consumed by worms that did not die.

2. I lamented and wept greatly over these things, for I was filled with sorrow on their account.

3. The angel said to me: "Why do you lament? Are you more merciful than God, who made all things and determined what was right for each?"

4. I answered the angel: "Will not the mercy of God prevail over these?"

5. The angel said to me: "What is it that you are saying? God is righteous in all his ways and just in all his deeds.

6. To each one according to their deeds he will render recompense.

7. The sinners will be punished for all eternity according to the hardness of their hearts, and they will have no rest in the fire even for a moment."

8. I marveled greatly at these words and said: "Righteousness and justice — who can stand before them?"

9. The angel answered: "No one can withstand the justice of God. Only those who received the grace of God in their lifetime and did the will of God will be saved."

10. I was greatly troubled by all that I had heard and seen, yet I glorified God the Father, who gives life to all and judges all in righteousness.

11. Then the Lord said to me: "Let us go now to the place of paradise and to the holy mountain."

12. And we went — I and my Lord — and he rejoiced greatly over me, and I also rejoiced greatly over him.

---
*LOGOS note: Peter's attempted intercession (v.4) parallels Abraham's intercession at Sodom (Gen 18) and sets a pattern for later apocalyptic intercession scenes. The angel's rebuke is categorical — not softened by later Universalist tendencies found in some manuscripts.*
